eli5: You bring your own key. The app uses your account, not ours, so nobody else sees or pays for your stuff.
english: Bring Your Own Key: you paste your own keys from online services. They stay on your computer, and each service bills you directly.
dev: Client-held provider credentials, encrypted locally with Electron safeStorage; calls go straight from the app to each provider, no proxy.

eli5: A secret password that lets an app use someone else's service, like a library card for a robot.
english: A private code that proves you may use an online service. Whoever has it can use your account, so keep it secret.
dev: Bearer credential sent with each request to authenticate and bill calls to a provider's API.

eli5: You can look at how the app is made, but there is one rule when you share videos made with it.
english: The code is public to read, but the licence is not a classic open-source one. Video Forge's rule is that published videos credit it.
dev: Published under the Forge Attribution License (FAL) v1.2, not an OSI-approved licence. Attribution on every publicly distributed Output is the core condition.

eli5: The rules for using Video Forge. The big one is saying "Made with Video Forge" when you share a video.
english: Forge Attribution License: free to use, even for paid work, as long as every published video credits Video Forge with the link.
dev: Forge Attribution License v1.2 (LICENSE). Free use; attribution with https://stravelakis.com/forge required on publicly distributed Outputs.

eli5: A sticker that says "free for everyone, no strings".
english: A licence that gives a work away to everyone. You can use it for anything, and no credit is needed.
dev: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 public-domain dedication.

eli5: The owner's own copy, with his own characters and music. Everyone else gets the public one.
english: A version of the app only the owner makes, with his brand packs, music and the 3D Humans. The public build is the one anyone can download.
dev: build-exe without --public: adds content linked in by npm run personal (private repo); separate appId; shares userData with Public.

eli5: The copy of the app anyone can download.
english: The version on GitHub Releases. It has the app, the drawn characters, 3D Mini people and 3D Pets, but no personal content.
dev: npm run build-exe:public; a guard (tools/lib/buildKind.mjs) refuses Mixamo-derived models and personal folders.

eli5: Windows says "I don't know who made this". Click More info, then Run anyway.
english: A warning Windows shows for programs that are not code-signed yet. It does not mean the file is harmful. Click More info, then Run anyway.
dev: Microsoft Defender SmartScreen prompt for unsigned or low-reputation executables. Signing via SignPath Foundation is planned.

eli5: A program with a stamp that says who made it.
english: Signed with a certificate that tells Windows who made the program. Video Forge is not signed yet.
dev: Authenticode signature on the .exe; absent in 0.4.0-beta.1.

eli5: A test version that is ready to try but not finished.
english: A GitHub release marked as a beta. It works, but it is not the final version yet.
dev: GitHub Release with prerelease=true; set by release.yml when the tag contains "-".

eli5: A name tag on one moment of the code, like v0.4.0, so everyone knows which version it is.
english: A label like v0.4.0-beta.1 put on the code. Pushing one builds the installer and the docs.
dev: Git tag vX.Y.Z[-beta.N]; triggers .github/workflows/release.yml and deploy-docs.yml.

eli5: A kit that turns a web page into a real app with its own window.
english: The framework Video Forge is built on. It runs web technology inside a normal desktop window.
dev: Chromium + Node.js desktop shell (v45 here), built with electron-vite and packaged with electron-builder (NSIS + portable).

eli5: A helper that lets your computer run the app's building tools.
english: A program that runs JavaScript on your computer. You need it only to build Video Forge from source.
dev: JavaScript runtime; the release build uses Node 22.

eli5: A shop that fetches the parts the app needs, and runs its little jobs.
english: The tool that comes with Node.js. It downloads the app's parts and runs commands like npm run dev.
dev: Node package manager; npm ci installs from package-lock.json, npm run <script> runs package.json scripts.

eli5: A tool that copies the project to your computer and remembers every change.
english: The tool for downloading (cloning) the code from GitHub and keeping track of changes.
dev: Distributed version control; git clone, branches, tags.

eli5: A window where you type commands instead of clicking.
english: A text window (PowerShell or Command Prompt on Windows) where you type commands such as npm run dev.
dev: Shell session; PowerShell on Windows. Env vars are set per session.

eli5: A guard that stops secrets from being saved into the project by mistake.
english: A free checker that looks for passwords and keys before each save to the project, and blocks the save if it finds one.
dev: Secret scanner run by githooks/pre-commit (gitleaks git --pre-commit --staged) and by secret-scan.yml in CI.

eli5: A tool that glues pictures and sound together into a video file.
english: A free program that joins, converts and cleans up video and audio. The installer brings a full copy.
dev: gyan.dev 9.0.2 essentials (GPL v3), pinned in tools/lib/ffmpegBundle.mjs. Picked in order: installer's own, full one on PATH, Remotion's bundled copy.

eli5: A tool that builds videos out of web pages, one picture at a time.
english: A video-making tool that draws each frame like a web page and turns the frames into a video file.
dev: React-based programmatic video framework (4.0.540); renders frames in headless Chromium.

eli5: A web browser with no window, used by the app behind the scenes.
english: A browser that runs without showing anything. The app uses one to draw the frames of your video.
dev: Chromium used for rendering; override its location with HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH.

eli5: A mouth shape that goes with a sound, so the character's mouth moves the right way.
english: One of a small set of mouth shapes used to animate speech. Video Forge uses nine, plus half-open in-betweens.
dev: Visual phoneme class; 9 base shapes (0 NEUTRAL to 8 CH_SH) plus in-betweens 10-12, held about 100 ms.

eli5: One big picture with nine faces, each making a different mouth shape.
english: A 3 by 3 grid of the same face with nine mouth shapes. The app flips between them while the character talks.
dev: 3072x3072 PNG, 3x3 grid of 1024 px cells; cell = index % 3, row = floor(index / 3).

eli5: A face cut into parts (mouths, eyebrows, eyelids) so it can move.
english: A puppet made from one portrait plus separate mouth, brow and eyelid pictures, with a file that says where each goes.
dev: <name>.rig.json + rig/<name>/*.png, built by tools/make-rig-puppet.mjs from base/ + layers/<name>/placement.json.

eli5: Asking an image AI to redraw only one small part of a picture.
english: Changing just one area of a picture with an image AI (here the mouth), so the rest stays exactly the same.
dev: Masked regeneration (Midjourney Vary Region, Photoshop Generative Fill, ComfyUI); merge back with tools/merge-mouth.mjs.

eli5: A note that says how to say a line, like "quietly". It is never read out.
english: Words in square brackets before the colon, like [in a hurry]. They tell the voice how to say the line.
dev: Bracketed prefix before the colon in Name [direction]: text; passed to directable engines, never synthesised.

eli5: One line of the script, and everything that comes from it.
english: One line of speech. It becomes one piece of audio, one or more subtitles, one scene and one moving mouth.
dev: NarrationSegment { speakerId, text, startMs, endMs, words? }; the unit for subtitles, visemes and background picks.

eli5: A way to measure how loud a video sounds, so all videos sound about the same.
english: A loudness unit. YouTube and TikTok aim for about -14 LUFS, so Video Forge sets the voices to that.
dev: Loudness Units relative to Full Scale (EBU R128). Two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP.

eli5: A colour recipe that makes the whole video look warmer, colder or like an old film.
english: A small file (.cube) that changes every colour in a set way. Colour packs sell or share them.
dev: 3D look-up table in .cube format, applied with FFmpeg lut3d plus eq for contrast and saturation.

eli5: The music gets quiet when someone talks, then comes back.
english: Turning the music down automatically while someone speaks, so the voice is easy to hear.
dev: Music gain reduced under narration, driven by the voice analysis.

eli5: How big the voice sounds, like a small cartoon or a big giant.
english: The part of a voice's sound that tells you how big the speaker is. Changing it makes a voice sound younger or bigger without changing the pitch alone.
dev: Formant shift in semitones (Rubber Band via FFmpeg); without rubberband the formants move with the pitch.

eli5: How many pictures flash by each second to make things look like they move.
english: The frame rate. More is smoother, but the file is bigger and slower to make.
dev: fps; Quick draft uses 3 fps at one third of the size.

eli5: A simple table saved as plain text.
english: A spreadsheet saved as plain text, with commas between the cells. Excel and Google Sheets can make one.
dev: RFC 4180-ish comma-separated values, UTF-8; parsed by electron/batch/sheet.ts, header names lower-cased.

eli5: A tidy text file that a computer can read easily.
english: A plain text file format for settings and data. Project files, puppets and brand packs are JSON files.
dev: JavaScript Object Notation.

eli5: A free AI that runs on your own computer, so nothing goes on the internet.
english: A program that runs AI models on your own computer. Image Forge's puppet maker can use it.
dev: Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible server (Docker), usually at http://127.0.0.1:8080.

eli5: A box that holds a program and everything it needs, so it runs the same anywhere.
english: A tool that runs programs in their own sealed box. LocalAI usually runs in one.
dev: Container runtime.

eli5: A common way for apps to talk to AI helpers, so many helpers can plug in.
english: The way most AI servers accept requests. Any server that speaks it (LM Studio, Ollama and others) works as "Your own server".
dev: OpenAI-compatible /v1 chat completions API; the base URL gets /v1 added if missing.

eli5: A voice that runs on your own computer. It is plain, but quick.
english: A free voice engine that runs on your computer. Flat but fast, good for checking timing.
dev: Local neural TTS (.onnx voices) run through a Python interpreter; no network, no per-use cost.

eli5: A voice that can act, like whispering or laughing, when you tell it to.
english: A voice engine that follows stage directions. It runs on a rented graphics machine, outside the app.
dev: Directable TTS on a rented GPU; stage directions steer the performance. Not synthesised inside the app.

eli5: A library of recorded body movements that can't be shared, so it stays in the owner's copy.
english: Adobe's library of recorded movements. Its rules do not allow passing it on, so the 3D Humans are only in the personal build.
dev: Adobe Mixamo animations; redistribution not permitted. models/animated/ and motions.json are gitignored and refused by the public build guard.

eli5: The part of a service you can use without paying.
english: An amount of use a service gives free, often per day or per month. Past it, it stops or starts charging.
dev: Provider quota without billing; limits vary per provider and model.
